cross_verdict: The set is sound on facts and limits, but it repeats itself across ads. Facts: every claim is on the allowed lists. Free shipping appears only on #19 and #21 (both over €100). Neither belt mentions an engraving. There are no banned words, emojis or exclamation marks. All fields were within limits before the edits and still are after them. The longest new primary_short is 23B at 215 characters, and every first 125 characters names the product, the material and (where it is not already on the creative) the price. The problems are repetition, plus one claim risk. (1) Three openers begin with "Nature" (23A, 19A, 19B). "By nature" is on #19's creative, so 19A keeps it, while 23A and 19B get new openers ("So the case you see on our site is the one we send." and "Smooth was never the point."). (2) 17A's "There is no second one." almost repeats #23's on-image "No second one exists.", and 17A's headline "one of one" echoes #21's "1 of 1." Both are replaced ("Down to the last scale."; "Pink Nile crocodile, gold buckle"). (3) "No two (are) alike" appeared in 16A, the 16B headline, 17B, the 19B headline and on #21's subline. It now stays only in 16A's primary_short, the long texts and #21's creative, and the other spots get different wording. (4) "Under the thumb" appeared in both 23B and 19A, so 23B becomes "smooth in the hand". (5) #23 said "the case you see / the one in the photo is the one you receive", which points at the ad image. #21 had already been fixed to point at the site photos. #23 now points at the site too, so the set is consistent and the promise is defensible. (6) 21A's preview never said "iPhone", and now it does. Remaining overlaps are acceptable. #23 and #21 share the photographed-individually promise because it is the same product fact, but the wording differs. 23B and 21A both open with short "Not…" fragments. You could also make "duties & taxes" vs "duties and taxes" consistent, but that is cosmetic. With these edits the set is ready to run.
